output.headline: An open platform in the target's sub-sector and a 2024 deal there make Advent a natural add-on buyer at $200M.
output.differentiator: One of three sponsors on the priority list with an open platform in the sub-sector (with Nordic Capital and Welsh Carson), and it pays a higher median multiple than Nordic Capital. [A:angles, T:record]

acquirer_overview.title: An established healthcare sponsor with a nine-year record and deep capital
points: 18 deals from 2016 to 2024, 15 closed (83%), across 9 active years; 17 of 18 (94%) were control deals. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:years_active, K:control_share]
Median deal of $124M, with 8 of 18 deals in the $100M-$400M size band that frames the target. [T:record, K:size_band]
Fund X of about $25 billion (2022 vintage) and approximately $100 billion AUM as of November 2025 give ample capacity. [P:1, P:2]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: An add-on to an open platform, backed by a provider record
points: Deals in this or neighbouring sub-sectors are a modest factor in its likelihood; deal count and size within its usual range are slight factors in favour. [S:sector_rel, S:activity, S:not_smaller]
Bought Crest Care Partners ($304M, 2024) in the target's own sub-sector, plus 7 deals in adjacent provider sub-sectors, 3 of them in Behavioral Health. [D:MA-2024-0120, T:record, K:by_sub_sector]
The open platform makes the target an add-on rather than a new bet; limited Midwest history is the one signal against. [A:angles, S:geo_fit]

precedent_activity.title: Recent same-sub-sector and behavioral health deals at comparable size
points: Crest Care Partners: $304M Recapitalization in 2024, closed, in the target's own sub-sector at 9.3x EV/EBITDA. [D:MA-2024-0120]
Crown Addiction Treatment ($123M Recapitalization, 2023, 14.6x) and Principal Counseling ($163M minority investment, 2021, 13.2x), both Behavioral Health. [D:MA-2023-0108, D:MA-2021-0341]
Summit DSO, a $303M Midwest Merger of Equals in 2018 at 11.7x; 5 deals since 2022 show continued activity. [D:MA-2018-0184, K:recent]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible and within Advent's own range
points: 70 comparable deals price at 10.7x EV/EBITDA (25th percentile), 12.8x (median) and 15.3x (75th percentile). [V:comps]
The target's 16.8% margin beats the comparables' 12.9% median and sits above 87% of them, justifying the 75th percentile. [V:comps]
Its median paid is 15.5x; IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target, and a platform exit supports up to $216M. [V:comps, V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: The same-exit maximum is $193M, below the $200M target, so the bid needs the add-on exit. [V:lbo, X:target]

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's region, and geography is a slight signal against. [T:record, S:geo_fit]
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal was Summit DSO, $303M in 2018, and Great Plains adds 3 deals. [D:MA-2018-0184, K:by_region]
risk_flags.reality: Regional familiarity is limited; the case rests on sub-sector fit and the platform. [A:angles]

risk_flags.title: Crowded process
risk_flags.concern: Ranks 9th on the priority list of 10, with a likelihood of 3.7%. [R:rank]
risk_flags.mitigant: The open platform add-on route and 5 deals since 2022 show intent. [A:angles, K:recent]
risk_flags.reality: Nordic Capital and Welsh Carson also hold open platforms and have more adjacent provider deals. [R:rank]

conviction.rationale: Rests on 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector, 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors, and an open platform add-on route. Its low list position reflects limited Midwest history, not weaker fit. [C:conviction, R:rank]
